evidence.quote: In situ TiC particles-reinforced FeCrNiCu high-entropy alloy matrix composites were prepared by vacuum induction melting method.

Note that dark round phase in Fig. 8d represents TiC particles, whose average diameter is approximately 1.611 μm.

Cu and Cu4Ti were identified from the corresponding XRD pattern shown in Fig. 3c.

Compared to Fig. 8c, the distribution of TiC particles becomes increasingly non-uniform as observed in Fig. 8d. The reason may be that the volume fraction is so large that the congregation of TiC particles occurs.

the content of Cu in the matrix is relatively low, and the segregation of Cu may occur at the grain boundaries.
there are a number of TiC particles, with severe contamination at the interfaces with the matrix, which may be ascribed to the poor wettability of the interfaces
